input: Create Key Points, a Study Guide, and Q/A Flashcards from this transcript excerpt: Token cost is an input to the solution cost, but reducing tokens is not the business outcome. Start with the value of the business process, subtract model, retrieval, platform, monitoring, and engineering costs, and verify that quality and safety remain above the release threshold.
expected: Key points identify tokens as one solution cost and define ROI as process value minus complete cost. The study guide connects token optimization to quality and safety gates, and the flashcards test the ROI formula and release conditions.
context: Token cost is one component of complete solution cost. Business ROI equals business-process value minus total solution cost, and optimization must preserve quality and safety.

input: Create Key Points, a Study Guide, and Q/A Flashcards from this transcript excerpt: Evaluation-driven development begins with a representative dataset and explicit release gates. Teams establish a baseline, change one routing or context decision, rerun the same evaluators, and release only when quality, safety, latency, and cost meet the agreed thresholds.
expected: Key points explain baseline-first evaluation and controlled changes. The study guide covers representative data and release gates, and the flashcards test when a change is safe to release.
context: Evaluation-driven development establishes a baseline and repeats the same evaluation after each controlled change.

input: Create Key Points, a Study Guide, and Q/A Flashcards from this transcript excerpt: The five design principles are route work to the smallest capable model, compress repeated context, retrieve only relevant evidence, cache stable prefixes or safe reusable responses, and simplify prompts, tools, and orchestration. These techniques should be measured together because saving tokens in one stage can move cost or latency elsewhere.
expected: Key points list routing, context compression, retrieval, caching, and simplification. The study guide explains end-to-end measurement, and the flashcards test each principle and why local savings can shift cost elsewhere.
context: The optimization principles are routing, context compression, retrieval, caching, and simplification, measured across the complete system.
